reason: Air seems the likeliest element to open a space within the primordial waters.
expectation: Air will create a void in the waters.

alternatives.reason: I could check which elements interact with the waters, but the opening suggests trying Air.

effect: Air opened the void, and the next goal is to put land there.
reaction: The image of a hollow opening in the deep is satisfying.
reason: Earth is the natural material for land, and the void is its intended location.
expectation: Earth will form land in the void.

effect: Earth formed a molten rocky world, and the goal now calls for daylight.
reaction: The hot, newly formed world makes cooling seem important later.
reason: Fire is the remaining element most suggestive of a source of daylight, so I will try it with the world.
expectation: Fire will create a light source for the world.

alternatives.reason: The void might instead be where the light source belongs.

effect: Fire cannot combine directly with the rocky world, but it can combine with the void or the deep.
reaction: The feedback makes the void the more promising place to try for daylight.
reason: Fire in the void may create the light source the world needs.
expectation: Fire will create a light source in the void.

alternatives.reason: The deep is also a listed partner, though its connection to daylight is less clear.

effect: Fire in the void created the Sun; daylight still needs to reach the world.
reaction: The image of a lasting light gathering in the void is satisfying.
reason: The Sun is the new light source, so pairing it with the rocky world is a direct way to pursue daylight.
expectation: Sunlight will reach the rocky world.

effect: The Sun illuminated the rocky world, and the next goal is a lesser light for night.
reaction: The ridges and hollows emerging from darkness are a vivid detail.
reason: I don't yet know what makes the lesser light, so checking Light's partners may reveal a useful route.
expectation: The partner list may suggest how to make a nighttime light.

alternatives.reason: The void was where the Sun formed, so it might also be involved in another celestial light.

effect: Light has no available combinations, so it does not directly lead to the lesser light.
reaction: That was not the clue I hoped for.
reason: The void was where the Sun formed, so inspecting it may reveal a route to another celestial light.
expectation: The void's available partners may suggest how to make the lesser light.

effect: The void has no available combinations, so it does not currently offer a route to the lesser light.
reaction: That rules out the place where the Sun formed.
reason: The rocky world may have a relevant partner for forming a lesser light, so I will check its available combinations.
expectation: Its partner list may suggest how to create the nighttime light.

alternatives.reason: The deep is another possible place to look for available reactions.

effect: The rocky world has no available combinations, so it offers no immediate route to the lesser light.
reaction: Another empty list is a little frustrating.
reason: Fire was previously shown to work with the waters of the deep, making that a known available combination worth trying.
expectation: Fire will produce something in the deep, though I don't know whether it will help make the lesser light.

alternatives.reason: I could check its current partners first, but Fire was already listed as compatible.

effect: Fire in the deep created a Starfield, but the lesser-light goal remains open.
reaction: The scattered reflections becoming distant fires are a striking image.
reason: The new Starfield may offer a route to the nighttime light, so its available partners are worth checking.
expectation: Its partner list may reveal how to make the lesser light.

effect: The Starfield has no available combinations, so it does not directly lead to the lesser light.
reaction: Another empty list is frustrating, though it rules out that route.
reason: The Sun is the other celestial light, so checking its partners may reveal a way to make the lesser one.
expectation: The Sun's available partners may suggest a route to the nighttime light.

alternatives.reason: The deep might have another available reaction.

effect: The Sun has no available combinations, so it offers no direct route to the lesser light.
reason: The waters of the deep produced the Starfield and may have another available reaction.
expectation: Its partner list may reveal a way to create the lesser light.

effect: Earth and the deep automatically made Sky stones, suggesting a possible material for the lesser light.
reaction: The scattered wandering bodies are an unexpected development.
reason: The new Sky stones may have a partner that leads to a moon or another nighttime light.
expectation: Their available partners may reveal how to make the lesser light.

effect: Sky stones struck the rocky world and formed the Moon, completing the lesser-light goal; the world now needs steadying.
reaction: The collision forming a companion that reflects sunlight was an interesting development.
reason: The Moon is the new companion, so checking its available partners may reveal how to steady the world.
expectation: Its partners may suggest a way to steady the world's turning.

effect: The Moon's gravity steadied the world's axial tilt, completing the final goal; its lean can still change over long ages.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the Moon have a further role beyond reflecting sunlight.

mostWorthwhile.text: Forming the Moon from a collision, then seeing its gravity moderate the world's tilt, connected the creation story to two useful ideas.

leastWorthwhile.text: The run of inspections returning empty partner lists was repetitive and made finding the next route frustrating.

surprise.text: Earth scattered through the deep became wandering sky stones, one of which struck the world and led to the Moon.

arbitrary.text: Casting Earth into the primordial waters to make sky stones was not an obvious route to a moon; I found it through inspection feedback rather than a clear inference.

continue.text: I would continue: the collision and the Moon's stabilizing influence made me curious about how the story will connect further making with real-world ideas, despite the repetitive searches.
